252778477_b8a24512.text: This model has recently been proposed to interpret the developmental origin of neuronal diversity in the hypothalamus (Zhang et al., 2020), which arises from the ventral diencephalon and contains an extreme heterogeneity of neurons that control endocrine, autonomic, and behavioral functions. Although we still do not have a satisfactory answer to how many neuronal subtypes there are in the vertebrate hypothalamus, recent unbiased mapping of neuronal identity by single-cell transcriptomic analysis has revealed at least 62 neuronal subtypes with different neurotransmitters and neuropeptides (Romanov et al., 2016)(Romanov et al., 2019)

252778477_34c9735a.text: .At the progenitor stage, hypothalamic NPCs lining the third ventricle are also supposed to be multipotent and homogeneous but can be subdivided into multiple cell states distinguished by either cell cycle gene sets or distinct transcriptional priming programs (Zhang et al., 2020)(Li et al., 2020). Importantly, these neural progenitors give rise to two major groups of IPCs with different transcriptional profiles, lineage specification, and spatial distribution, which are each marked by the transcription factors Ascl1 and Neurog2 (Zhang et al., 2020)

252778477_1ec938aa.text: .In striking contrast, Ascl1 + and Neurog2 + IPC domains in the hypothalamus coexist in a mosaic but mutually exclusive pattern.
